extraction_notes:
BUNDLE: 'labels' - 10 source keys covering 18 approved oligonucleotide products, all US prescribing information (HL7 v3 SPL XML from NLM DailyMed, US public domain).

PARSING HAZARD 1 (MATERIAL - CHANGES A SEQUENCE). The tag-stripped .txt sitting beside each DailyMed XML is NOT a faithful rendering. For inotersen (S12) the .txt DROPS ONE 3'-terminal [2'-O-(2-methoxyethyl)]m5rC residue from the section 11 chemical name, producing a 19-mer that contradicts the label's own P19S19 molecular formula. The XML prints all 20 residues. Every sequence and every per-position modification row here was read from the XML. Anyone re-deriving inotersen's sequence from the .txt will get it wrong.

PARSING HAZARD 2 (MATERIAL - SCRAMBLES TABLE VALUES). The .txt flattens SPL <table> elements so that row labels and cell values are separated by unrelated text. In the imetelstat .txt, for instance, 'PTT prolonged' appears next to a stray '7' that belongs to a different row. All table-derived numbers here (imetelstat Tables 5 and 6, inotersen Table 2, olezarsen Table 1, nusinersen Table 3) were obtained by parsing the XML <tr>/<td> structure with an XML parser. For those rows the verbatim_quote is the table ROW LABEL, because SPL stores each number in its own cell with no surrounding sentence; the cell values and their column headers are spelled out in the row's notes and source_locus. This is a deliberate, disclosed limitation of quoting tabular SPL data, not a missing quote.

CROSS-VALIDATION OF THE PER-POSITION CHEMISTRY. Three labels (inotersen S12, eplontersen S68, donidalorsen S46) print a full residue-by-residue chemical name, and imetelstat (S20) prints a uniform one. I parsed each and then checked the resulting phosphorothioate count against the sulfur count in the label's OWN stated molecular formula: inotersen 19 PS vs S19; eplontersen 13 PS + 6 PO vs S13; donidalorsen 15 PS + 4 PO vs S15. All three matched exactly, so these modification rows are validated against the source rather than assumed. Nusinersen and tofersen describe their architecture but print no bases (tofersen's are in a figure), so they get no modification rows.

AN UNPLANNED FINDING WORTH THE REVIEWER'S ATTENTION. The triage packet said 'sequences: no' for every label in this bundle. That is wrong for four of them. Reading section 11 of S12 and S68 side by side shows that inotersen and eplontersen carry the IDENTICAL 20-base sequence (UCUUGGTTACATGAAAUCCC) and the IDENTICAL 5-10-5 MOE sugar pattern, for the same target and indication. Their differences are backbone (19/19 PS vs 13 PS + 6 PO), GalNAc conjugation and dose (284 mg weekly vs 45 mg monthly). The S12-vs-S68 contrast is therefore a genuinely sequence-controlled comparison, verified from the labels rather than inferred, which strengthens the negative control considerably.

DIRECTION CONFLICT THAT MUST SURVIVE AGGREGATION (imetelstat, S20). All-grade PTT prolongation is HIGHER on drug (26% vs 18% placebo) but Grade 3/4 PTT prolongation is LOWER on drug (1% vs 4% placebo). These are two separate rows with opposite effect_direction values from the same table. Any pipeline that collapses all-grade and high-grade into a single direction will misrepresent this label. Note also that the label writes 'PTT' and defines it as partial thromboplastin time; it never writes 'aPTT', so readout_name preserves 'PTT'.

GRANULARITY CONFLICT RESOLVED CONSERVATIVELY (nusinersen, S52). One triage sweep graded this label per_compound_numeric. I confirmed the conservative reading: every number in this label is a PLATELET count. Searching all coagul*/prothrombin/thromboplastin occurrences returns only the class-attribution sentence, the section 2.4 monitoring mandate, the section 5 summary, the section 6 cross-reference and the section 17 counselling text - not one PT or aPTT value anywhere. For the clotting-time endpoint this label is qualitative. Its PT and aPTT rows are recorded as MONITORING MANDATES with readout_value NOT_REPORTED, explicitly flagged so they can never be mistaken for results.

ABSENCE VS MEASURED NULL - THE DISTINCTION IS ENFORCED IN THE DATA. Two different things are recorded and they must not be merged:
  (a) REGULATORY SILENCE (15 rows, sources S68-S72): the label never raises the endpoint. effect_direction is NOT_REPORTED on every one of these rows, and an assertion in the build script enforces that no row from a negative source can carry a measured direction. I re-verified all the zeros myself over both the XML and the text, and the two keyword false positives (patisiran 'thrombophlebitis' as an extravasation sign; nedosiran 'If there is bleeding, lightly press a cotton ball...' as Instructions-for-Use advice) are recorded as their own explicit rows so a downstream keyword grep cannot promote them.
  (b) BOUNDED NEGATIVES / MEASURED NULLS (olezarsen S45, donidalorsen S46, nusinersen S52): the sponsor looked and reported nothing. These carry effect_direction 'no_change'. Where the label states the zero in words ('There were no major bleeding events...', 'no DAWNZERA-treated patient had a platelet count of <50,000/mm3') I set readout_value NOT_REPORTED rather than inventing a '0', because no numeral is printed.

PLATELET ROWS ARE SCOPE-LIMITED. Platelet count alone belongs to the separate thrombocytopenia endpoint. Platelet rows appear here only where the source itself ties the finding to a bleeding or haemostatic outcome in the same passage; they are categorised platelet_coag_crosstalk and every one carries an explicit scope caveat in its notes. They are included because they are the exposure variable for the paired bleeding negatives (olezarsen, donidalorsen) and for the haemorrhage rows (inotersen), not as coagulation measurements in their own right.

ON-TARGET VS UNINTENDED. Only donidalorsen's prekallikrein rows are on_target_effect=true: it is the only approved oligonucleotide that deliberately knocks down a contact-pathway zymogen. Note those are plasma CONCENTRATION (antigen) reductions, not clotting-factor ACTIVITY assays, and the label reports no aPTT or other clotting time despite lowering a contact factor by 73%.

UNRESOLVED / FOR THE REVIEWER. (i) Imetelstat's 'hemorrhage (2.5%)' serious-adverse-reaction rate is numerically identical to its 'Grade 3 or 4 bleeding 2.5%' rate but the two use different definitions; the label does not say whether they are the same patients, and I did not merge them. (ii) Inotersen has a second DailyMed label in the corpus (Catalent, setid 3d31f4c0-...) that was not in this bundle and was not compared. (iii) inclisiran's label silence conflicts with a small external trial reporting real FVIII and fibrinogen falls; that tension is flagged on the inclisiran row itself.

ENUM COMPROMISES, DISCLOSED. Imetelstat's sugar is 3'-amino-3'-deoxyribose, which the sugar_mod list does not contain; recorded as 'DNA' (it is 2'-deoxy) with the 3'-amino substitution carried by backbone_linkage_3p 'PN', and the whole reasoning written into every basis string. Its oligo_class is 'other' for the same reason. PMO and GalNAc-siRNA products got NO per-position rows: their chemistry is uniform, so a per-position table would add nothing beyond the sequence string, and the phosphorodiamidate morpholino linkage has no correct value in the backbone_linkage_3p list - forcing it into 'PN' would have made it indistinguishable from imetelstat's thio-phosphoramidate. Their uniform chemistry is captured losslessly in the oligo-level backbone_chemistry ('PMO_neutral') and sugar_modifications fields instead.
refused_rows:
1. NUMBERS THAT EXIST ONLY IN FIGURES. Eteplirsen (S71) and viltolarsen (S71) print 'the structure and base sequence' only as an image; patisiran, givosiran, lumasiran, inclisiran, vutrisiran, nedosiran and plozasiran (S70, S72) print their sequences only in a structural-formula image. Tofersen (S69) states its 5-10-5 architecture and 15 PS / 4 PO linkage split in text but puts its bases in Figure 1. In every case I set sequence_5to3_asprinted and sequence_base to NOT_REPORTED and emitted no modification rows. No figure was read.

2. A CHEMISTRY I COULD HAVE COPIED FROM A SIBLING PRODUCT BUT DID NOT. Olezarsen's (S45) section 11 in this SPL version prints no chemical name, no sequence and no molecular formula. It is the same sponsor and the same GalNAc-2'MOE class as donidalorsen, whose full per-position name I did parse, and the published olezarsen structure is well known. I left backbone_chemistry, sugar_modifications, gapmer_design, conjugate and ps_count all NOT_REPORTED, because carrying chemistry across from a sibling product is exactly the kind of plausible inference this dataset must not contain.

3. A LENGTH I COULD HAVE DERIVED. Nusinersen's (S52) label never states its length. P17S17 in the stated formula implies an 18-mer, and the literature agrees, but the label does not say it, so length_nt is NOT_REPORTED.

4. INOTERSEN'S INJECTION-SITE REACTION RATE (49% vs 10% placebo, Table 2). Its footnote lists component terms 'bruising, erythema, hematoma, hemorrhage, induration, ...'. Three of those are bleeding terms, but they are pooled into a single local-tolerability composite with seven non-bleeding terms and no per-component rate is printed. Extracting it as a bleeding_outcome would have been the single largest 'signal' in the bundle and would have been wrong. Refused. The clean bleeding row from that same table (Contusion, 7% vs 2%) is extracted instead.

5. AN ATTRACTIVE CROSS-LABEL ARITHMETIC. Imetelstat's placebo arm shows a HIGHER Grade 3/4 PTT rate than the drug arm (4% vs 1%), which invites computing a protective effect. I recorded both rows with their printed values and opposite directions and did not compute, net, or reconcile anything. Likewise I did not compute attributable risk differences beyond restating the two printed percentages in effect_vs_control.

6. SEVERITY GRADING. I assigned no severity grade anywhere. severity_stated_by_source contains only the source's own words ('Grade 3 or 4', 'life-threatening', 'sudden severe thrombocytopenia', 'All Grades'), verbatim, for central grading against the written rubric.

7. TURNING REGULATORY SILENCE INTO A MEASURED NEGATIVE. The strongest temptation in this bundle. Thirteen coagulation-silent labels across five negative sources would make thirteen tidy 'no effect' rows. They are recorded instead as NOT_REPORTED with effect_direction NOT_REPORTED, and the build script asserts that no row from S68-S72 can carry a measured direction. A label that never mentions coagulation is evidence about REGULATORY ATTENTION, not about coagulation.

8. PLATELET-ONLY ROWS WITH NO HAEMOSTATIC TIE. Inotersen's Table 2 'Thrombocytopenia 24% vs 2%' adverse-reaction row and its baseline-stratified nadir statistics (39% vs 6%), and nusinersen's High Dose Regimen platelet statement, are pure thrombocytopenia findings with no bleeding or coagulation-cascade readout attached in the same passage. They belong to the thrombocytopenia dossier and were left there.
